"'''Hands to Heaven'''" is a [[Sentimental ballad|ballad]] by English band [[Breathe (British band)|Breathe]], taken from their debut studio album, ''[[All That Jazz (Breathe album)|All That Jazz]]'' (1987). The song was released as the band's fifth UK single on 20 October 1987 by [[A&M Records]] and as their second single in the United States the following year. It was written by group members David Glasper and Marcus Lillington and produced by [[Bob Sargeant]]. The B-side of the single features an instrumental track, "Life and Times".

"Hands to Heaven" became Breathe's breakthrough international hit. The single peaked at {{abbr|No.|Number}} 4 on the [[UK Singles Chart]] in August 1988.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Search {{!}} Official Charts |url=https://www.officialcharts.com/search/True%20Love/?artists=0&albums=0&films=0 |access-date=2025-10-31 |website=www.officialcharts.com}}</ref> In the United States, it spent two weeks at No. 2 on the [[Billboard Hot 100|''Billboard'' Hot 100]] during the same month. The song also reached No. 2 on the [[Adult Contemporary (chart)|''Billboard'' Adult Contemporary chart]].<ref>Hyatt, Wesley (1999). ''The Billboard Book of #1 Adult Contemporary Hits''. Billboard Publications.</ref> Additionally, "Hands to Heaven" reached the top 10 in Canada, Ireland, New Zealand, and Norway.

"Hands to Heaven" is a ballad by English band Breathe, taken from their debut studio album, All That Jazz (1987). The song was released as the band's fifth UK single on 20 October 1987 by A&M Records and as their second single in the United States the following year. It was written by group members David Glasper and Marcus Lillington and produced by Bob Sargeant. The B-side of the single features an instrumental track, "Life and Times".

"Hands to Heaven" became Breathe's breakthrough international hit. The single peaked at {{abbr|No.|Number}} 4 on the UK Singles Chart in August 1988. In the United States, it spent two weeks at No. 2 on the Billboard Hot 100 during the same month. The song also reached No. 2 on the Billboard Adult Contemporary chart. Additionally, "Hands to Heaven" reached the top 10 in Canada, Ireland, New Zealand, and Norway.

sections.heading: Music video
sections.wikitext: The music video for "Hands to Heaven" was directed by Eamon McCabe and features the band in a surreal, dreamlike sequence. It begins with lead singer David Glasper falling asleep in the back of a black London taxicab, drifting into a series of dreamlike visuals. Throughout the video, the band is shown performing in softly lit, stylized settings, while the surroundings shift among blurred city streets, the cab interior, and abstract performance backdrops. The muted color palette, soft transitions, and reflective cinematography emphasize the song's themes of longing and romantic separation. The video concludes with Glasper waking up in the cab and being driven away by the same driver, completing the narrative loop.

sections.heading: Personnel
sections.wikitext:
'''Band'''
* David Glasper – vocals
* Marcus Lillington – guitars, keyboards
* Ian "Spike" Spice – drums
* Mike Delahunty – bass

'''Guest musician'''
* Paul "Shilts" Weimar – saxophone

'''Production'''
* Arranged by Breathe
* Engineer: John Madden ("Hands to Heaven", "Stay")
* Mixing: John Madden ("Life and Times"), Chris Porter ("All That Jazz")
* Remixing: Chris Porter ("Hands to Heaven")
